findings.title: OffsetTracker partition-lock creation is racy
findings.body: In src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:49 _get_partition_lock() does get() then setdefault() on self.partition_locks with no lock. Two worker/submit threads creating the same new Partition can create two different Lock objects and then use different locks to guard all_offsets/outstanding/last_committed. Consequence is lost mutual exclusion, corrupted offset sets, and committing an offset whose predecessors are still outstanding, causing message loss on restart.

findings.title: Unbounded queues contradict claimed backpressure
findings.body: In src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:185 FixedQueuePool creates plain queue.Queue() with no maxsize and submit() in line 204 just puts. poll() never blocks. The class docstring claims natural backpressure, but the Arroyo poll loop can enqueue without bound if one group stalls. Consequence is unbounded memory growth/OOM instead of slowing the Kafka consumer, defeating the stated goal of isolating slow items.

findings.title: Shutdown cannot drain and depends on Queue.shutdown
findings.body: In src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:231 shutdown() sets worker.shutdown=True then calls q.shutdown(immediate=False). OrderedQueueWorker.run() in line 129 loops while not self.shutdown, so after the flag is set it exits after the current item instead of draining. Also queue.Queue.shutdown only exists on Python 3.13+; on older runtimes it raises AttributeError which is swallowed, leaving workers blocked forever in get(). Consequence is either dropped queued work on graceful shutdown or hung/leaked worker threads and a join storm.

findings.title: Failed items are still marked complete and committed
findings.body: In src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:149 OrderedQueueWorker.run() calls offset_tracker.complete_offset() in finally unconditionally, and ResultProcessor.__call__ already swallows all exceptions. The strategy docstring promises only commits after successful processing, but any exception still advances the contiguous committable offset. Consequence is poison-pill / transient DB failures are acked and never retried, silently losing uptime results.

findings.title: Shared queue pool is destroyed by one strategy close
findings.body: In src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/result_consumer.py:133 the factory creates one FixedQueuePool shared by every SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy returned from create_with_partitions, but in src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:335 SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()/terminate() shuts down that shared pool and join() calls close(). On rebalance or multi-partition assignment closing one strategy kills workers/queues for all other live strategies reusing the same pool. Consequence is stalled consumption after the first rebalance requiring process restart.

findings.title: Offsets committed from background thread
findings.body: In src/sentry/remote_subscriptions/consumers/queue_consumer.py:273 SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy._commit_loop runs on its own thread and calls the Arroyo Commit callable and mark_committed(). Arroyo expects commit to be driven from the processing strategy poll/join path; concurrent commits race with partition revocation and with other strategies sharing the same OffsetTracker. Consequence is committing offsets for revoked partitions, double commits, or missing the final commit on close, breaking at-least-once guarantees.
